results.title: Stable economy, cheaper credit key to youth jobs — BoG Governor
results.content: The Governor of the Bank of Ghana (BoG), Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama, says falling lending rates and stronger private sector credit growth are among the gains from recent macroeconomic management efforts, creating improved conditions for businesses to access financing and expand operations.

results.title: BoG turns to AI to strengthen financial-sector oversight
results.content: The Governor of the Bank of Ghana (BoG), Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama, has called for a dedicated digital platform to make the country’s official statistics more accessible, saying wider access to reliable data could improve economic research, policymaking and investment decisions.

results.title: The Breast that feeds the future: Nurture it, Protect it, Check it
results.content: Why breastfeeding and breast cancer are one story, and why women and men must both read it In the first hour of life, a mother’s breast delivers colostrum, the baby’s first vaccine. Over the next six months it can supply everything a child needs. It is one of the most powerful public health tools we have. It is also the site of the cancer most often diagnosed in Ghanaian women, and, surprisingly, one that men can get too. This is one organ and one story: how we nurture it, how we protect it, and why we must keep checking it.

results.title: Anas announces exposé on Angela List’s Nguvu/Konongo Mines
results.content: Investigative journalist Anas Aremeyaw Anas is preparing to publish an investigation into the operations of Nguvu/Konongo Mines, owned by Angela List, with a focus on the dispute surrounding the mining interests and its possible implications for Ghana’s gold sector.

results.title: Leonant Yert retains position as Most Outstanding PR Agency
results.content: Leonant Yert Ltd has been named the “Most Outstanding Public Relations Agency (PR Consultancy of the Year)” for the 2025 review period at the 2026 Institute of Public Relations (IPR), PR Ghana Excellence Awards. This latest recognition strengthens Leonant Yert’s position as the leading Public Relations consultancy in Ghana and validates the Firm’s previous winning of the same award for the 2023-2024 review period. The back-to-back recognition also underscores the Consultancy’s commitment to delivering strategic communication, reputation management, issues and crisis management and stakeholder engagement solutions that create measurable value for its clients.

results.title: Communications Minister Sam George confirmed as chair of AU STC on Communication and ICT
results.content: Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George (MP), has been confirmed as Chair of the African Union Specialised Technical Committee on Communication and ICT (AU STC-ICT) at its 6th Ordinary Session in Libreville, Gabon.

results.title: Patrick Stewart, best known for “Star Trek” and “X-Men,” dies at 86
results.content: Legendary actor Sir Patrick Stewart, best known for his work in the "Star Trek" and "X-Men" franchises and his prolific award-winning stage career, has died at 86 years old, his spokesperson confirmed.

results.title: Court remands four over Worawora disturbances
results.content: The Dambai Circuit Court has remanded four people to police custody over their alleged involvement in disturbances at Dwabrem-Worawora in the Oti Region.

results.title: Dr. Bawumia confers with KAS Secretary-General; discusses Ghana’s future and NPP reorganisation
results.content: Former Vice President and NPP Presidential Candidate, Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia, has held high-level talks with the Secretary-General of the Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung (KAS), Dr. Mark Speich, in Accra on Thursday. KAS is one of Germany's leading political foundations and is internationally affiliated with the NPP.

results.title: Ghana targets $1.2bn investment and 150,000 jobs under new textile policy
results.content: Ghana is targeting about $1.2 billion in investment and 150,000 direct and indirect jobs over the next decade under a new textile and garment policy approved by Cabinet. The policy, which is expected to be formally launched by the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, also seeks to expand the country's textile and garment industry from an estimated $400 million to about $2 billion. It further aims to revive domestic cotton production across 50,000 hectares as part of efforts to strengthen local raw material supply and support the growth of the industry. The targets were announced by the Trade Ministry’s Director of Research, George Amoah, at the launch of the second phase of the International Labour Organization’s (ILO) Productivity Ecosystem for Decent Work programme. results.title: Google value plunges by $500bn as AI fears rattle Wall Street
results.content: Google parent Alphabet lost just over $500bn (£374bn) in value on Thursday after it rattled Wall Street with its last update of the year on its business operations.

results.title: UPSA Graduates 1,314 Students at 18th Congregation
results.content: The University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA), on Wednesday held the third session of its 18th Congregation at the Kofi Ohene Konadu Auditorium, where 1,314 students from the Faculty of Management Studies graduated. Various awards were presented to students who excelled.

results.title: Three held over Momo Vendor ‘s murder at Kasoa
results.content: The Central East Regional Police Command has arrested two persons and a juvenile in connection with the alleged murder of a mobile money vendor at a guest house near Kasoa in the Central Region.

results.title: Russell Brand’s wife tells his rape trial he is ‘kind and a wonderful father’
results.content: Russell Brand's wife Laura has told a court her husband is "caring, kind and a wonderful father to our children".

results.title: Businessman in court for allegedly defrauding colleague of $3.5m
results.content: An Adenta Circuit Court has granted bail to a businessman allegedly involved in a US$3.5 million fraud case.

results.title: Ten missing manhood cases false; Police vehicle vandalised at Breman
results.content: The Asankragwa Divisional Police Command has dismissed 10 reported cases of alleged missing manhood in its operational area as false, following medical examinations that confirmed the complainants’ genitalia were intact and medically normal.

results.title: Israeli opposition accuses Netanyahu of trying to ‘delegitimise’ election
results.content: The main Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot and Arab-led party leaders have denounced Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for alleging foreign interference following the election which saw his coalition lose its majority.

results.title: George Michael’s Faith guitar sells for £180k after auction row
results.content: The guitar George Michael performed with in his 1987 Faith music video has sold for £180,000 at auction, after a row over the sale of memorabilia related to the singer.

results.title: 47 university students attend first Unmute Yo’Self public speaking event in Accra
results.content: Forty-seven university students have participated in the first edition of Unmute Yo’Self, a free public speaking and confidence-building event aimed at helping young people communicate their ideas more effectively. The event was held on Friday, October 23, 2026, at the Accra AI Community Center in Ridge, Accra. Organised by the Sincerely Accra Podcast in collaboration with The Gold Coast Report (GCR), the programme was sponsored by Malta Guinness and Ashesi University. Participants included students from first year through to their final year. The initiative was designed to address the challenges young people face in expressing themselves confidently in classrooms, job interviews and professional settings.

results.title: Philippine police obtain warrant to search Thomas Markle’s devices
results.content: Philippine police have obtained a warrant to examine devices seized from the former home of Thomas Markle, father of the Duchess of Sussex.

results.title: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17bn deal it says will expand customer options
results.content: DoorDash will acquire grocery delivery firm Instacart in a $17bn (£12.8bn) deal, creating a behemoth that will bring more meals, quick-need purchases and big weekly shops directly to customers.

results.title: Trade Ministry launches pharmaceutical policy to double local medicine production
results.content: The government has launched the Cabinet-approved Ghana Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Policy, seeking to double domestic medicine production, create skilled jobs and position the country as a leading pharmaceutical manufacturing hub in West Africa.

results.title: Ghana woos Polish investors with access to African markets
results.content: Ghana has urged Polish and other European businesses to invest in the country, citing its democratic stability, access to African markets and improving economic conditions as key advantages. The Deputy Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Sampson Ahi, made the call during a panel discussion on “What Investors Need to Know from Both Governments” at the TOP CHARITY ChangeMAKERS Africa Business Mixer in Accra. He said Ghana’s stable democratic environment, respect for the rule of law and growing middle class made it an attractive destination for investors seeking to expand their operations. Mr Ahi also highlighted Ghana’s role as host of the Secretariat of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), describing it as a strategic advantage for businesses seeking access to the wider African market. results.title: Health Minister assures public of Ghana’s readiness to respond to Ebola
results.content: The Minister of Health, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, has assured the public that Ghana is prepared to detect and respond to any potential Ebola case, following an inspection of screening and emergency response measures at Accra International Airport.

results.title: Health Minister urges contractors to speed up La General Hospital project
results.content: The Minister of Health, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, has urged contractors working on the La General Hospital project to accelerate construction to meet the scheduled commissioning deadline of January 2028.

results.title: Responsible mining must be the standard, not the exception – Dr Zanetor Rawlings
results.content: The Minister for Environment, Science and Technology, Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, has called for responsible mining practices to become the standard in Ghana, stressing that mineral extraction must not come at the expense of the environment.

results.title: African CEOs remain confident in growth, but economic uncertainty, AI readiness will shape next phase of investment – KPMG
results.content: The findings point to a business environment in which ambition remains strong, but execution is becoming increasingly important. While 66% of African CEOs are confident in the global economy, broadly in line with the global benchmark of 65%, confidence in their domestic economies stands at 72%. A further 79% are confident in the growth prospects of their own organisations.

results.title: MTN’s profit before tax for Q3 hits GH¢ 11.3 billion
results.content: The figure represents a 51.8% jump over the GH¢ 7.7 billion it recorded during the same period in 2025.

results.title: 5th Edition of Ghana Corporate Brands Conference and Honours launched
results.content: Under the theme, "Shaping the Future of Corporate Branding in Ghana: Building Brands with Strategic Intent, Inspiring Excellence, and Earning Lasting Trust", the event is expected to convene key voices from business, academia and industry to discuss emerging branding trends, reputation management, customer expectations and the growing role of technology in shaping public perception.

results.title: NAIMOS targets suppliers of equipment used in illegal mining in Aowin and Enchi
results.content: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) has announced plans to target individuals and businesses manufacturing or selling equipment used in illegal mining as part of efforts to curb galamsey in Aowin and Enchi in the Western North Region. Director of Operations at NAIMOS, Colonel S. K. Appiah, said the taskforce would focus on the supply chain supporting illegal mining activities in addition to enforcement against operators. Speaking during a tour of the taskforce’s operations in the area, he said the objective was to enforce the law and halt the destruction of the environment without unnecessarily undermining legitimate livelihoods. “We are not here to destroy livelihoods, but to enforce the law,” he said.
